resolutions.researcher_notes: Value 'operating' supported indirectly: Saudipedia (Saudi govt encyclopedia, independent of GEM) says the Hawiyah Gas Plant was completed in 2001 and is operating, recovering non-associated sour gas from the al-Khuff/al-Jawf reservoirs; euro-petrole (reprint of Aramco's own release) describes the Haradh/Hawiyah Khuff-gas development as an operating Aramco system. Neither names this specific 43 km Haradh Khuff -> Hawiyah trunk line, so 'operating' is inferred from the parent gas plant/field being onstream. Note GEM maintains a separate newer entry 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah 3 gas pipeline' (2023 compression increment); this P1917 is the original older line.

Fuel=Gas is unambiguous. Saudipedia describes the Hawiyah plant processing non-associated sour gas from the al-Khuff reservoir; euro-petrole/Aramco describes the Haradh & Hawiyah gas development. Two independent sources both confirm this is a natural-gas (Khuff) system.

No independent source could be found stating a 43 km length for this specific Haradh Khuff -> Hawiyah line. The only figure of '43 km / 27 miles' appears on GEM and GEM-mirroring pages (offshore-technology data-insight page actually describes a DIFFERENT, later line: 450 km / 36 in / Eastern Province / ops 2024, per GlobalData). Trade sources (OGJ) give only aggregate gas-transmission totals (e.g. 130 km across five 20/30-in Haradh lines; 2,718 km total for the Haradh/Hawiyah/Uthmaniyah increment), not this segment. Cannot verify 43 km.

No independent source confirms a 30-inch diameter for this specific line. '30 in' appears only on GEM/mirrors. OGJ notes Haradh-area gas transmission uses a mix of 20-inch and 30-inch lines, which is consistent with but does not specifically corroborate 30 in for this 43 km segment. Cannot verify 30 in.

Confirms Saudi Arabia + Hawiyah (Al Hawiyah) gas plant endpoint fed by Haradh Khuff gas. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: GEM lists EndState/Province='Makkah', but the Hawiyah Gas Plant sits in the Eastern Province (South Ghawar area / Jubail industrial zone per Saudipedia), NOT Makkah. 'Makkah' most likely a mix-up with the town of Al Hawiyah near Taif in Makkah Province, which is unrelated to this gas facility. Recommend Update correct EndState/Province to Eastern Province.

Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100% well supported: Saudipedia states the Hawiyah Gas Plant is operated by Saudi Aramco within its Master Gas System; euro-petrole/Aramco identifies the Haradh & Hawiyah gas development as a wholly Saudi Aramco project. All Saudi upstream gas infrastructure is Aramco-owned. Two independent sources agree.
